Not a big fan of the "real time" battles because I have to pause every second to make sure the team doesn't get stuck or gets wrecked by an AOE spell. I didn't feel compelled to play the DLC as I approached the end and unfortunately once you beat the ending of the main story you don't get to go through and play the DLC you have to do that before you beat the game. But the story is good and the party characters a enjoyable to be around.

If only I'd chosen a different class, maybe I would have been more useful to my own group. Horribly dull character the hunter. Good thing that the rest of the group compensated for my lack of good abilities, except... for the huntress that joined later. Hunters aside, the story was deep and interesting, somewhat original, the mechanics were pretty decent (maybe the recommended difficulty was too easy, but, well, I guess I could replay on a higher difficulty) The rotation of gear on my characters was not quite exciting, I ended up playing the whole game with the same bow, but what the heck, if it works ¿? At least the game had other elements to it and the wide range of abilities for magic users were satisfactory. The lore was amazing (I ended up following only conversations because honestly I got lost on so much unnecessary lore, but it was great nonetheless) The conversations where deep (sometimes too deep and felt like I was drowning into metaphors) but all in all, the game felt very enjoyable. I think I might even replay it in the future, but probably I'll get into the other titles that Obsidian has to offer. Honestly I'm looking forward to see what improvements they've made on those, and based on this game, the other games must be pretty good (Tyranny and PoE2). But back to this, I tottally recommend this game! Just, don't play a hunter!

A good RPG. 7/10

The overall feeling I got from this game was a good one, however there were some mechanics that I either did not understand or were not that great.

The whole economy and crafting system is broken. I was loaded with cash and with materials that were worthless. I did not find the potions/food/scrolls of any use.
For me it was very difficult to compare item quality.
Some classes have very, very, very scarce skill options (ranger, warrior, etc.). They are basically right click auto-shoot.
The story was very slow at the beginning / mid game.
The lore is too complex or the names are just too complicated. Very easy to get confused.

The music is fantastic and the artwork is on point.
Characters backstory was pretty good, with some exceptions.
The overall combat mechanics are pretty interesting.
Has a very high replay value due to almost unlimited build trees.
Great game. Would also recommend the DLC. Combat can be frustratingly hard, micromanaging every little detail can be exhausting but playing on normal difficulty will smooth the entire experience.
Classic CRPG though a bit too wordy, story and characters are better than DOS, but the combat can get overly tedious, though.

Excellent game. Those who loved the original Baldur's Gate series will definitely enjoy this, despite the different mechanics. It brings sense of nostalgia but also does enough to make it its own game. The different mechanics may take some getting used to, and you will definitely want to play on Fast-Mode outside of battle as the running animations are very slow on normal speed, but the world-building and combat mechanics are both top-notch. I love the dialogue options and the NPCs as well. Highly recommended!
If you like Baldur's Gate 1 or 2, Icewind Dale, etc. this is worth picking up.

My only gripe with this game would be with its technical aspects -- the obnoxiously long loading times and its unbelievably huge filesize. The rest is great, and I can't recommend this game enough. Praised be Eothas.
phenomenal storytelling, great voice acting, and hours of gameplay. Loved every minute of this game

Ehhhh....this one's difficult. I'm recommending it, but I didn't like it, and not everyone will. I can admire this game, I definitely can, but it's way too hardcore for me. If you want a really hardcore RPG then this is for you, but I think I'll just stick to Bethesda
Slow to get into, but if you give it time it becomes a world and story worth knowing. The gameplay is dated, but the writing more than makes up for it.

An in depth and overall well made game.

In my expirience it crashed quite a bit, but there are ways to get around it.
Love this game. Top tier CRPG with tons to do and some of my favorite characters in gaming. Solid main and side stories with choices that feel like they have real impact on them.

A good and extremely well written game marred by schizophrenic and at times outright unfair difficulty which turns the late game and the expansions into a joyless, miserable slog. Enemies will come in vast swarms that envelop your party and hit you with endless status effects to constantly paralyse, petrify, knock down or terrify your party members, making combat confusing and incredibly annoying. I found myself playing the same obnoxious encounters over and over again, and I got through them only to have my max level party repeatedly one shot by certain bosses. I'm not saying that the difficulty is insurmountable, I'm saying it's frustrating and tedious and that I stopped enjoying the game a good ten hours before I stopped playing. I kept hoping it would get better, but I just got more miserable, and I honestly cannot work up the motivation to actually finish. I don't think it's a bad game, the world is rich, the art is nice and the mechanics are good, but the latter half of it is such a joyless experience I couldn't finish it and I can't in good faith recommend it.

A masterpiece. Everything I loved about the old Baldur's Gate games, but with massively improved QoL and mechanics designed from the ground up for a computer game as opposed to a TTRPG. If you like CRPGs, this is a must-play.
Classic Isometric style RPG a la Baldur's gate, icewind dale. Different ruleset slightly. Works well, although load times are reminiscent of baldur's gate when it first came out. Enjoyable overall.

An interesting game, similar to BG 1 & 2. So it's a lot of fun. Mainly bug free too.
The only strange challenge was playing in a none turn based game. So the solution is pause, set the characters off doing their thing and pause again to change opponents or strategy.

I would like to thank all the bakers and Obsidian for this great CRPG.
PoE has it all: REALLY different classes and builds, skill checks, class checks, great companions, art and story, choices that matters and have consequences.
DLCs (WM1 and WM2) are also very good and on par with main game (sometimes are even better)!

Keep it up Obsidian! I hope PoE 2:Deadfire will be also as cool or better as original PoE.

Thanks a lot, make CRPGs great again!
Amazing game. Great story, wonderful characters and voice acting, engaging combat. One of my favorite games.

This game is awesome, super compelling. I found the interface and controls a little confusing at first, but I love the way your decisions impact the story. I'm also a huge fan of games that let you completely design your character (backstory and all!) This is the kind of game I would have completely lost my mind over as a kid.

This rating is based on preference.

While the worldbuilding was cool, the delivery of the narrative was in shambles. I felt myself struggling to appreciate the story and characters. There were interesting aspects to the classes, and plenty of unique ways to play them, but the gameplay just didn't do it justice (the skills just feel so bad, im sorry).

The best thing about this game, by far, is the non-story lore. Unfortunately, I didn't like how it was presented, and found myself often trying to dig for it.

Lots of things to like, but the attention this one got baffles me. There are many better crpgs to play, especially if you crave a meaningful story.

Though, the ending was great, completing this game felt like a chore to me.

An excellent CRPG with amazing lore. I finally finished it (after 120+ hours..!?) and can't wait to jump into PoE II. It gets easy towards the end but, I found that rewarding because of the hard battles I'd fought through early on in the game. Didn't care if the endgame was a cakewalk but it's all about the story anyway!

Absolute masterpiece <3
Personally not a huge fan of the pause based combat system. I prefer Turn based, but I loved it every step of the way.
the main game is amazing but unfortunately i really hated the dlc, which kinda ruined the whole experience for me. still recommend it as long as you don't touch the white march

I showed up for the Baldur's Gate/Icewind Dale flashbacks and stayed for Obsidian's intriguing love letter to Ye Olde Fantasy CRPG. Who needs sleep?

Yes, Pillars of Eternity is worthy of your attention--and you don't need to know where Minsc hides Boo to enjoy your time in Eora.

(Due to an endless supply of life stuff and an ineffable compulsion to wander aimlessly, I've started multiple characters across multiple platforms many times. With any luck, I'll soon manage to follow through on one of my misadventures through this lovingly-crafted universe.)

Pillars of Eternity was expressly created as an homage to the Infinity Engine games; the interface and beautiful painted backgrounds definitely make it look the part. But what made games like Baldur’s Gate, Icewind Dale, and Planescape so special was more than just an aesthetic: they were vast, sprawling settings with epic stories that delivered engaging tactical encounters. And when judged by those criteria, I feel that Pillars of Eternity is a worthy successor to carry on the legacy of the Infinity Engine. Though the loss of the AD&D engine and settings does take some getting used to, the mechanics are solid and the world is compelling and fun to discover. It’s an easy recommendation for fans of of the Infinity Engine and I’d also recommend it for anyone interested in an engrossing quest through a fantastic land.

If this is your first Realtime With Pause game, it's going to take some adjustment, and I fully suggest picking an easy to manage class as micro-managing might turn you off from the gameplay. Once you adjust to it and get into the game's groove however, it becomes so much more fun. If you like CRPGs, or are interested in them, hell maybe even if you just like character customization and dialogue options, this might not be the best starting point, however it is still one of the best modern day CRPGs, and I wholeheartedly suggest giving it a try.
Why god is there so much combat in this game. I'm lvl 4 and probably killed a 100 enemies. Every level of the first couple dungeons is just jam packed with tiring endless combat.

"A whore wants neither praise nor devotion. A whore wants to be compensated for her services, and Magran is paid and pleasured in sweat and struggle and pain. This... mewling imbecile is unworthy of Magran's womanly heat." - my waifu

Pillars of Eternity is a shining example of what an RPG should be. It has immense depth in both gameplay and story. It uses its own flavor of Dungeons and Dragons-esque ruleset; establishes its own races, nations, and monsters; and presents it all in a familar and accessible formula that spells fun any way you slice it. It has a very managable user interface that stands far above the old days of Infinity Engine gameplay while not sacrificing that intricate feel of the games of old. The graphics are picturesque paintings of fantasy settings where your 3D sprites will move about - I did find myself wishing for more character customization options though. Pillars of Eternity is a love letter to pen and paper, Infinity Engine, and fantasy RPG fans alike.

A modern Baldur's Gate. Writing, gameplay mechanics, everything is simply excellent. Finished on the very hardest difficulty, which is not recommended for most players. The last boss is a damage sponge like nothing you've ever seen.

Another point is the excellent customization, while they do take their freedoms in intrepreting and making their own "DnD rulesets", especially for health and encumbrance, you'll get to terms to it eventually. May be hard to grasp in the beginning. Outside of this there's a ton of lore, areas to explore, secrets to find and gorgeous environments to wander in that makes you lose track of time. Cannot be recommended enough.

Rating: 10/10!
Enjoyable game. A story worth following. Good character diversity. The load screens are a bit long for how frequent they are.

Pillars of Eternity introduces its players to a gorgeous new world with a fascinating story to tell, along with an interesting new combat system. A word of caution: combat is difficult and Pillars suffers from a bad case of "tell, don't show". In other words, if you're a fan of the old Forgotten Realms games and enjoy reading Tolkien, this game will be right up your alley. If either of those works make you want to flip a table, this probably isn't the game for you.

A challenging RPG with fantastic voice acting and action-packed gameplay, Pillars of Eternity will not disappoint fans of the genre. Obsidian Entertainment has "WOW"d me twice, the first by way of South Park, a solid RPG that was actually fun to play. PoE is very different in style and design; it has that fantasy appeal... very Bard's Tale'ish.

Pick it up & enjoy!
This game cured my gaming fever, it has a great story, interesting companions, enjoyable combat. Love it.

It took me a few tries to get into this game, but once it clicked, I found that it was a blast! I didn't much care for the combat - it was very janky and hard to grasp for me, but despite that, this is one of the best RPG's I've played in recent years. I've done just about everything there is to do in the game in one playthrough (a lot of my playtime was offline via Steam Deck, so hours weren't counted), and it was a joy from start to finish. Be warned, there is A LOT of reading, and if you are planning on skipping dialogue and rushing through the game, you will not have fun.
Its just very good. Story kept me hooked the whole time and I like the combat mechanics too. Art style runs on nostalgia, but the quality is top.
Play this one before the second. I liked the second better but this is still one of the best crpg game series if you are into crpgs. Worth a buy.

Even though I'm hardly a fan of RTwP, I quite enjoyed the game. It's well-balanced, you can set up the characters' behaviour in the battle, the story is captivating enough. However, some of the companions seemed a bit flat and the main character's motivation as thought up by the developers was a bit vague, that's why some of the dialogue options later on might have come up as a surprise. Despite that, all in all, it's a nice game, worth a playthrough

A very good game that has issues. Overall the gameplay is really solid and rewarding. There is a ton of spells and abilities to learn with some real rewarding experiences. That said there is is a ton of micro management here that can really get on your nerves. Some things don't seem fair either and I have run into hard road blocks that made me go back to previous saves. If you are not ready for something you just die. Still very good game that I would recommend.

Masterpiece! :D

Not much more to say. If you're looking for a well-written, multi-choice, story-driven adventure/RPG, this is it! I finished the end-game first time today, including the White March expansions, and enjoyed (almost) every minute of it.

The only improvements I can think of right now are:
* Loading screens took too long. For travelling from A to B, then into house C and into room D, that you'd already explored, you'd sometimes have to sit by four loadings screen. Easier ways to travel would have been appreciated.
* The keep management was a nice addition to the game, but felt a bit "shallow". More ways to customize the keep, that made difference for defense and reputation would have been nice.
* I felt that to immerse even more into the world, it would have been nice to see more rewarding side activites, i.e. more than 'throwing dart' or 'playing dice' at the local tavern. I think this could have improved the replayability of the game, and also provided some extra variation to the chain of "interrogate - explore - battle".

Bottom line? Great game! Very fun to play. I was always a HUGE fan, and played nearly all of, the early Dungeons and Dragons games (Baldur's Gate I&II, Icewind Dale I&II, etc...). This game is touted as a spiritual successor to these games and truer words have not been spoken! If you like isometric RPGs, this is the game for you!

Pillars of Eternity is an RPG much like Baldur's Gate 1. The world is interesting and the action is fun. I recommend this game for people who like to follow a story, statagize small party combat and level up your characters. Owning and managing a stronghold is also fun and adds to the game depth.

So far so good.

A heartfelt thank you to the creators for such a soulful and deep journey. The world is rich, the companion stories are truly memorable, and the quest design is top-tier. Thoughtful party and resource management made every choice matter. A true classic for any RPG fan.

Simply put, I love this game. The soundtrack is spectacular and the artwork is stunning, especially for a CRPG. The world is interesting and diverse and it is a wonderful time-sink. If you need to scratch that classic D&D itch; then this is probably a great game for you. 9/10.

Pillars of Eternity (along with its two expansions) is an incredibly addictive game. It's easy to lose yourself in the game world, and as soon as I completed the game, I started planning what my next character would be. If you have a fondness for RPG games, you can't go wrong with this one.

It took me a while to get my head around the magic system in PoE, but great game play and exceptional story and dialogue in this game. Not just your average hack n slash game and I highly recommend PoE if you love a good story and interesting NPC's.

If you're familiar with Baldur's Gate, Pillars of Eternity will evoke feelings of nostalgia. Same point and click gameplay, but built using a new engine. The character sprites are one of the best improvements as their detail has been drastically enhanced. The environments are varied and you will always be curious as to what's next. Tons of sidequests, a stronghold you can build, great characters and dialogue and toooooons of story and lore. You will become fully versed in a world you never knew existed. Pillars of Eternity is worth every penny!

tldr.text: Very Positive (88%): players love the story and characters, and many also enjoy the combat.
The story and characters also draw the most complaints, with many finding the quest pointless after a few hours.

details.text: Recent reviews are slightly more positive than the all-time score, at 91% positive.
Players who review in their first hours are far less positive, with only 56% positive, and one reviewer says the game "feels uninteresting" after a few hours.
